summary: Dedicated pool latency spikes during model rollout (all-at-once update saturates reserved capacity); request staged rollout controls
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports a sharp latency/timeout regression during a model rollout on their Dedicated reserved pool. They believe the issue correlates with our current “all-at-once” pool update behavior.

Customer / Tenant
- Company: Northlake Financial
- Tenant: northlake-prod
- Dedicated pool: dp_us_east_northlake_01 (reserved)

Impact
- Elevated p95 latency and intermittent timeouts on their primary chat route.
- Customer states they have internal SLA targets and this event triggered an incident on their side.

Environment
- Deployment: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool)
- Region: us-east
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (streaming)

Timeline (customer-provided)
- 2025-01-14 13:05–13:20 UTC: initiated model update (pin moved from 2024-12-18 -> 2025-01-13).
- 2025-01-14 13:08 UTC: p95 latency began rising.
- 2025-01-14 13:10–13:16 UTC: worst window; frequent queueing and timeouts.
- 2025-01-14 13:18 UTC: customer reverted model pin to previous version; latency recovered over ~3–5 minutes.

Observed symptoms (customer)
- “Requests stuck waiting before first token” during the rollout window.
- Streaming connections timing out more frequently than normal.

Requested
- Ability to do staged/canary rollouts on Dedicated pools (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic gating on latency/timeouts/queue depth.
- Ability to require a manual approval between stages.

Notes
- This appears consistent with reserved pool saturation during a full-pool rollout / cache warm-up behavior. We should confirm queue depth and utilization at the pool level and whether any autoscaling guardrails were hit.

Customer attachments
- Customer provided timestamps and request IDs via email; pasted into comments for privacy reasons (no file attachment).
comments:
2025-01-14T15:02:11Z | Dev Patel (Support) -> Customer
Thanks for the detailed timestamps. We’re pulling pool-level metrics (queue depth, GPU utilization, timeout rate) for dp_us_east_northlake_01 during 13:00–13:30 UTC. Can you confirm whether the rollout was a model pin change only, or did you also change any runtime parameters (max_batch_tokens, kv_cache settings, concurrency limits)? Also, if you can share ~10 request IDs that timed out, we can trace them end-to-end.

2025-01-14T15:19:44Z | Customer (Northlake Financial)
Rollout was a model pin change only. No config changes. Request IDs (timed out): req_7c2f…, req_80a1…, req_9b44…, req_1e02…, req_5a9d…, req_f3d8…, req_3f0c…, req_6b91… (full list shared with Owen via secure channel).

2025-01-14T16:01:27Z | Owen Phillips (Support Engineer)
Initial look at dedicated pool metrics suggests queue depth and GPU utilization spiked immediately after the model version pin changed. p95 ‘time_to_first_token’ rose sharply for ~8 minutes, then recovered after revert. This pattern looks like a pool-level saturation + warm-up effect (plus increased compute per token on the newer build).
Next steps: (1) confirm if new model build has different default context limits/kv-cache behavior, (2) check whether rollout triggered simultaneous restarts across the pool, (3) correlate timeout spikes with evaluator/routing events.

2025-01-14T16:22:13Z | Sean Gallagher (SRE) (Internal)
Pulled dashboard: dp_us_east_northlake_01 utilization hit ~97–99% during the window; queue depth peaked ~4–6x baseline. 5xx didn’t spike significantly; this is mostly queuing/timeouts. I think this is exactly why we need staged rollouts for Dedicated + minimum headroom guardrails. Linking internal initiative for product/eng visibility.

2025-01-14T16:28:40Z | Dev Patel (Support) -> Customer
We can reproduce the pattern on our side: no major 5xx increase, but a pronounced queue depth and time-to-first-token spike coincident with the model pin change. For immediate mitigation: please continue using the previous pinned model until we can validate the new build under load. If you need to move forward sooner, we can coordinate a low-traffic window and temporarily lower route concurrency to maintain headroom during the update.
We also have an in-flight project to add staged rollouts + gating for Dedicated pools; we’d like to include Northlake as a design partner if you’re open to it.

2025-01-15T10:12:09Z | Customer (Northlake Financial)
Yes, we’re open to being a design partner. We need: (a) canary traffic split on the pool, (b) auto-pause/rollback on latency/timeouts, (c) audit trail of who approved the rollout step. We can’t keep doing big-bang updates on reserved pools.

2025-01-15T12:03:55Z | Owen Phillips (Support Engineer)
Root cause hypothesis: the 2025-01-13 model build has a slightly higher per-token compute cost for Northlake’s typical prompt lengths, reducing effective throughput. During the pool update, the combination of (1) restart / cache cold-start behavior and (2) reduced throughput pushed the pool into sustained queueing until the revert.
Workaround options:
1) Keep model pinned to 2024-12-18 for now.
2) If upgrading is required, do a controlled window: reduce concurrency on the route by ~20–30% for 15 minutes during/after the change, and avoid other changes.
3) We can optionally provision temporary burst capacity (if available) during the change window.
Action: I’m filing an internal request to add Dedicated staged rollout support for exactly this failure mode and will attach metrics evidence from this incident.

2025-01-16T09:41:22Z | Marcus Lin (Security) (Internal)
Customer request includes approval audit trail. Please ensure support messaging aligns with planned audit events (create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold) and retention. We should route this to the audit logging workstream as well.

2025-01-17T17:26:10Z | Dev Patel (Support) -> Customer
Closing the loop: We’ve confirmed this was queueing/throughput saturation during an all-at-once Dedicated pool update (not an error-rate event). Current mitigation is to keep the previous model pin or coordinate an upgrade window with reduced concurrency to maintain headroom.
We’ve logged your requirements (staged rollout weights, gating on latency/timeouts/queue depth, manual approvals, and audit trail). Our product/engineering teams are actively building Dedicated staged rollouts; we’ll follow up separately to schedule a short design session and discuss beta timing.
resolution: Mitigated by reverting model pin to prior version; confirmed saturation/queueing during all-at-once Dedicated pool update. Provided operational workaround (upgrade window + temporary concurrency reduction). Captured customer requirements for Dedicated staged rollouts with gating + approvals + audit trail and linked to internal delivery workstreams.
next_steps: Support/CS: schedule design partner session with Northlake (staged rollout requirements + success criteria). SRE/Eng: validate newer model build throughput for Northlake prompt distribution; propose safe rollout procedure until staged rollouts are available. Product: include this incident as a motivating example for Dedicated staged rollout gates (latency/timeout/queue depth) and approval auditability.
customer_visible_summary: During a model update on your Dedicated reserved pool, we observed a temporary but significant increase in queue depth and time-to-first-token latency that aligns with our current all-at-once update behavior. Reverting the model pin restored performance. As a near-term mitigation, we recommend either keeping the previous model pinned or coordinating an upgrade window with reduced concurrency to maintain headroom. We’ve also recorded your request for staged/canary rollouts with gating and approval audit trails, and will follow up on beta participation.
